The '''2021–2022 United Kingdom censuses''' collectively comprised the 23rd [[census]] of the [[United Kingdom]].

The censuses of [[England and Wales]], and [[Northern Ireland]] took place on 21 March 2021, and the census of [[Scotland]] took place later on 20 March 2022.<ref name="ReleasePlans">{{cite web |url=https://www.ons.gov.uk/census/censustransformationprogramme/census2021outputs/releaseplans |title=Release plans: Our proposed plans for the release of Census 2021 data and analysis |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=24 May 2022 |website=ons.gov.uk |publisher=Office for National Statistics |access-date=29 May 2022 |archive-date=29 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220529205644/https://www.ons.gov.uk/census/censustransformationprogramme/census2021outputs/releaseplans |url-status=live }}</ref> The censuses were administered by the [[Office for National Statistics]] (ONS) in England and Wales, by the [[Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency]] (NISRA) in Northern Ireland,<ref>{{Cite web|title=2021 Census|url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/census/2021-census|url-status=live|access-date=5 November 2020|website=[[Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170703182652/https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/census/2021-census |archive-date=3 July 2017 }}</ref> and by the [[National Records of Scotland]] in Scotland.

These were the first UK censuses for which most of the data was gathered online.<ref>{{Cite web|title=About the census|url=https://census.gov.uk/about-the-census/|url-status=live|access-date=5 November 2020|website=Census 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200521123709/https://census.gov.uk/about-the-census/ |archive-date=21 May 2020 }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=27 March 2014|title=The census and future provision of population statistics in England and Wales: Recommendation from the National Statistician and Chief Executive of the UK Statistics Authority, and the government's response|url=https://www.ons.gov.uk/census/censustransformationprogramme/beyond2011censustransformationprogramme/thecensusandfutureprovisionofpopulationstatisticsinenglandandwalesrecommendationfromthenationalstatisticianandchiefexecutiveoftheukstatisticsauthorityandthegovernmentsresponse|url-status=live|access-date=5 November 2020|website=[[Office for National Statistics]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925032823/https://www.ons.gov.uk/census/censustransformationprogramme/beyond2011censustransformationprogramme/thecensusandfutureprovisionofpopulationstatisticsinenglandandwalesrecommendationfromthenationalstatisticianandchiefexecutiveoftheukstatisticsauthorityandthegovernmentsresponse |archive-date=25 September 2020 }}</ref> Two of the censuses went ahead despite the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], in part because the information obtained would assist government and public understanding of the pandemic's impact.<ref>Office for National Statistics, [https://census.gov.uk/about-the-census/the-census-during-the-coronavirus-pandemic The census during the coronavirus pandemic] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210201184238/https://census.gov.uk/about-the-census/the-census-during-the-coronavirus-pandemic |date=1 February 2021 }}, accessed 30 January 2021</ref> The census in Scotland was postponed, and took place in 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/scottish-news/scottish-census-what-is-what-26351143 |title=Scottish Census: What it is, what it means and how to complete once-a-decade survey |last=Phoutinane |first=Ketsuda |date=26 February 2022 |website=Daily Record |publisher=Reach plc |access-date=3 March 2022 |quote= |archive-date=3 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220303174427/https://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/news/scottish-news/scottish-census-what-is-what-26351143 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=17 July 2020|title=Coronavirus: Census delayed by a year because of disease|work=[[BBC News]]|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-53444651|url-status=live|access-date=5 November 2020|archive-date=15 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201115235002/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-53444651}}</ref>

The censuses in 2021 and 2022 follow on from [[Beyond 2011]], a project by the [[UK Statistics Authority]] to assess the value, cost, and alternatives to running a census in England and Wales in 2021. The project recommended an England and Wales census be held in 2021, and that it be conducted predominantly by means of online returns.<ref name=":0" />

Initial results for England and Wales were released on 28 June 2022, while initial results for Scotland were released on 14 September 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/about/2022-census/census-outputs-schedule/ |title= Census outputs schedule |website= Scotland's Census|publisher=[[National Records of Scotland]] |access-date=17 May 2025}}</ref>

== Background ==

[[File:Census 2021 message by the First Minister of Wales; Welsh Government video.webm|thumb|An explanation by [[Mark Drakeford]], the [[First Minister of Wales]], on how the census results will help to inform the decisions made in [[Wales]] and help to "make Wales a more equal country."]]
After the [[United Kingdom Census 2011|2011 census]], both the [[Cameron–Clegg coalition|UK coalition government]] and the main opposition party, [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]], expressed concerns about the rising costs of the decadal census. There were also concerns about the value of continuing with the traditional approach adopted for the 2011 census. This included whether collection methods were still fit for purpose in a rapidly changing society and whether census outputs, based on a survey conducted every ten years, would continue to meet the increasingly demanding needs of public and private sector users. Emerging technological developments were seen as providing alternative and improved data gathering opportunities. These concerns and opportunities led the UK Government to question if a supplementary or wholly alternative approach to the traditional 10-yearly census was required; more frequent, possibly annual, small-scale surveys could be employed instead.<ref name="Beyond2011background">[http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/background-to-beyond-2011/index.html Background to Beyond 2011 Office for National Statistics website] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131126154346/http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/background-to-beyond-2011/index.html |date=26 November 2013 }}, Ons.gov.uk, Retrieved 30 April 2014</ref>

In 2011, [[The Beyond 2011 Programme]] was established to look at alternatives to the traditional census approach. The UK Statistics Authority coordinated the project which was also undertaken by its counterparts in the devolved administrations of [[Scotland]] and [[Northern Ireland]].<ref name="2021recommendation">[http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/beyond-2011-report-on-autumn-2013-consultation--and-recommendations/index.html The census and future provision of population statistics in England and Wales: Recommendation from the National Statistician and Chief Executive of the UK Statistics Authority 27 March 2013] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151110133828/http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/beyond-2011-report-on-autumn-2013-consultation--and-recommendations/index.html |date=10 November 2015 }}, Ons.gov.uk, Accessed 23 April 2014</ref>

In 2014, the UK Statistics Authority announced the recommendation from the Beyond 2011 Programme that there should be a decennial-style 2021 census in England and Wales, which in contrast with earlier censuses, would be conducted predominantly through online completion of census forms, supplemented by the further use of administrative and survey data. Existing census gathering methods would be used only as an alternative, where online methods are not feasible.<ref name="Beyondrecommendation">[http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/beyond-2011-report-on-autumn-2013-consultation--and-recommendations/index.html The census and future provision of population statistics in England and Wales UK Statistics Authority published 27 March 2014] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151110133828/http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/beyond-2011-report-on-autumn-2013-consultation--and-recommendations/index.html |date=10 November 2015 }}, Ons.gov.uk, Accessed 1 April 2014</ref> A parallel announcement for Scotland's 2021 census was made by the National Records for Scotland.<ref name="BeyondrecommendationGROS">{{Cite web |url=http://www.gro-scotland.gov.uk/press/2014/plans-for-a-census-in-scotland-2021.html |title=Plans for a Census in Scotland in 2021 National Records for Scotland Press Release 27 March 2014 |access-date=1 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407080648/http://www.gro-scotland.gov.uk/press/2014/plans-for-a-census-in-scotland-2021.html |archive-date=7 April 2014 |url-status=dead  }}</ref> The ONS Director, Population and Demography Statistics was reported as saying that an estimated 60–65% of household returns would be completed online.<ref>[http://www.statslife.org.uk/features/1423-report-from-counting-the-population-the-2021-census-and-beyond-event  Report from ‘Counting the population: the 2021 Census and beyond’ event 1 May 2014] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140508030743/http://www.statslife.org.uk/features/1423-report-from-counting-the-population-the-2021-census-and-beyond-event |date=8 May 2014 }}, Accessed 7 May 2014</ref>

In April 2014, the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|British House of Commons]] [[Public Accounts Committee (United Kingdom)|Public Accounts Committee]] (PAC) concluded in its report ''Too soon to scrap the Census'', that the 2021 census should go ahead. It had reservations over the lack of investigation into the options for using administrative data and encouraged the UK Government to reassure the public about privacy concerns.<ref>[https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm201314/cmselect/cmpubadm/1090/109007.htm ''Too soon to scrap the Census'' – UK Parliament Public Administration Committee Report Published 9 April 2014] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161027171711/http://www.publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm201314/cmselect/cmpubadm/1090/109007.htm |date=27 October 2016 }}, Publications.parliament, Accessed 1 May 2014</ref>

The [[Minister for the Cabinet Office]] welcomed the recommendations for a predominantly online 2021 census for England and Wales supplemented by the use of governmental and other administrative data in a letter to the National Statistician in July 2014. He made clear that the Government saw the dual-running decennial national census with administrative data gathering option as a transitional approach and asked the National Statistician to ensure sufficient research is undertaken both prior to and after the 2021 census to find and validate alternative methods to replace the traditional national census and intermediate surveying approach.<ref>[http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/reports-and-publications/beyond-2011-research-conference-2014--summary-of-proceedings.pdf Beyond 2011 Research Conference 2014: Summary of proceedings – August 2014] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903120913/http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/reports-and-publications/beyond-2011-research-conference-2014--summary-of-proceedings.pdf |date=3 September 2014 }}, Ons.gov.uk, Accessed 31 August 2014</ref>

=== Legislation ===

Under the [[Census Act 1920]], it is for the [[United Kingdom Government]] and [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|Parliament]] to determine the arrangements for census-taking in England and Wales. Parallel legislative procedures will be required in the devolved administrations of Scotland and Northern Ireland. It would be late 2015 at the earliest before regulations were made. Subject to this legislation being passed the census would be conducted on the same day in England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland to ensure coherence and consistency.<ref name="2021recommendation" /> There is a legal requirement to complete the 2011 census questionnaire, under the terms of the Census Act 1920. As at 21 March 2021 everyone who had lived or intended to live in the country for three months or more was required to complete a questionnaire. Failure to return a completed questionnaire could lead to a fine and criminal record.{{citation needed|date=May 2024}}

In Scotland, the [[Census (Amendment) (Scotland) Act 2019]] made provisions for voluntary questions about [[transgender|transgender status]] and [[sexual orientation]] to be asked.<ref>{{cite web |title=Holyrood backs new census questions on transgender identity |url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2019/jun/13/holyrood-backs-new-census-questions-transgender-identity |last=Brooks |first=Libby |date=13 June 2019 |website=[[The Guardian]] |accessdate=6 October 2019 |archive-date=5 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191005174646/https://www.theguardian.com/society/2019/jun/13/holyrood-backs-new-census-questions-transgender-identity |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[Census (Return Particulars and Removal of Penalties) Act 2019]] makes the same provision for England and Wales. The sexual orientation question would also be asked in Northern Ireland.<ref name="Cooley2020">{{cite journal|last1=Cooley|first1=Laurence|title=Sexual orientation and the 2021 UK census|journal=European Journal of Politics and Gender|year=2020|volume=3|issue=3|pages=445–447|issn=2515-1088|doi=10.1332/251510820X15845548424385|s2cid=216328507|url=http://pure-oai.bham.ac.uk/ws/files/93846395/Sexual_orientation_and_the_2021_United_Kingdom_census.pdf|access-date=3 April 2022|archive-date=11 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511155452/http://pure-oai.bham.ac.uk/ws/files/93846395/Sexual_orientation_and_the_2021_United_Kingdom_census.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Guyan2021">{{cite journal|last1=Guyan|first1=Kevin|title=Constructing a queer population? Asking about sexual orientation in Scotland's 2022 census|journal=Journal of Gender Studies|year=2021|pages=1–11|issn=0958-9236|doi=10.1080/09589236.2020.1866513|doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== Religion ===

The campaign 'If you're not religious, say so!' by [[Humanists UK]] aimed to change the wording of the census question on religion. This campaign encouraged non-religious people to tick 'no religion' in order to create a more accurate portrayal of religiousness in the UK.<ref>{{Cite web|title=If you're not religious, say so! Tick 'No religion' in the 2021 Census|url=https://humanism.org.uk/census-2021/|access-date=2 March 2021|website=Humanists UK|language=en|archive-date=1 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301160421/https://humanism.org.uk/census-2021/|url-status=live}}</ref>
Another campaign by the Climate Census campaign group suggested writing in 'Climate concerned' in response to the religion question, to demand climate action from the government.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Declare yourself Climate Concerned|url=https://climatecensus.uk/|access-date=10 March 2021|website=Climate Census|language=en|archive-date=4 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210304100412/https://climatecensus.uk/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== <span class="anchor" id="sex controversy"></span>Legal challenge to 'What is your sex' guidance ===

The Office for National Statistics published an online guidance titled ''What is your Sex'' for the 2021 census. The guidance provided that a respondent should answer according to official documents such as their passport. [[Gender self-identification|Self-identification]] is already recognised in some countries. A gender marker on a British passport can be changed in a less formal procedure than acquiring a legally enforceable [[Gender Recognition Act 2004|gender recognition certificate]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Change your name or personal details on your passport |url=https://www.gov.uk/changing-passport-information/gender |access-date=25 March 2023 |website=GOV.UK |language=en}}</ref> 
	
In March 2021, Fair Play for Women, an [[anti-transgender movement in the United Kingdom|anti-transgender]] campaign group against self-identification,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=McLean |first=Craig |date=2 November 2021 |title=The Growth of the Anti-Transgender Movement in the United Kingdom. The Silent Radicalization of the British Electorate |journal=International Journal of Sociology |volume=51 |issue=6 |pages=473–482 |doi=10.1080/00207659.2021.1939946 |issn=0020-7659|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=25 September 2018 |title=It's now or never to defend female rights - here's why |url=https://fairplayforwomen.com/backgrd/ |access-date=26 March 2023 |website=Fair Play For Women |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jones |first1=Charlotte |last2=Slater |first2=Jen |date=July 2020 |title=The toilet debate: Stalling trans possibilities and defending 'women's protected spaces' |journal=The Sociological Review |language=en |volume=68 |issue=4 |pages=834–851 |doi=10.1177/0038026120934697 |issn=0038-0261|doi-access=free |hdl=10871/121533 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> applied for judicial review in England and Wales and argued that such incidental self-identification should not be allowed in census-taking.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Greenhalgh |first1=Hugo |date=17 March 2021 |title=UK gov't concedes defeat to Fair Play For Women in census sex row |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/britain-lgbt-government-idUSL8N2LF3D8 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726044355/https://www.reuters.com/article/britain-lgbt-government-idUSL8N2LF3D8 |archive-date=26 July 2021 |access-date=26 July 2021 |website=Reuters |language=en}}</ref><ref name="bbc1">{{Cite news |date=9 March 2021 |title=Census 2021: Judge orders change to sex question guidance |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-56338666 |url-status=live |accessdate=10 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310000104/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-56338666 |archive-date=10 March 2021}}</ref> In the absence of opposition or intervention from any interested party, the judge ordered an interim revision of the guidance.<ref name="bbc1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 March 2021 |title=Guidance on sex question in census must be changed, high court rules |url=http://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/mar/09/guidance-on-sex-question-in-uk-census-must-be-changed-high-court-rules |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310191428/https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2021/mar/09/guidance-on-sex-question-in-uk-census-must-be-changed-high-court-rules |archive-date=10 March 2021 |accessdate=11 March 2021 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref> The government conceded and accepted the order. The ONS withdrew from the High Court proceedings.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lyons |first=Izzy |date=17 March 2021 |title=ONS backs down on 'what is your sex?' Census legal dispute |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2021/03/17/ons-backs-sex-census-legal-dispute/ |url-status=live |access-date=20 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210319205319/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2021/03/17/ons-backs-sex-census-legal-dispute/ |archive-date=19 March 2021}}</ref>
	
[[Alice Sullivan]] criticised what she said was the ONS's confusion between the concepts of sex and gender identity.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sullivan |first1=A. |year=2020 |title=Sex and the census: Why surveys should not conflate sex and gender identity |url=https://doi.org/10.1080/13645579.2020.1768346 |journal=International Journal of Social Research Methodology |volume=23 |issue=5 |pages=517–524 |doi=10.1080/13645579.2020.1768346 |s2cid=219471164|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Other academics supported the design of the census questions,<ref name="Fugard pp. 525–531">{{cite journal |last=Fugard |first=Andi |date=25 May 2020 |title=Should trans people be postmodernist in the streets but positivist in the spreadsheets? A reply to Sullivan |url=https://eprints.bbk.ac.uk/id/eprint/31812/10/31812a.pdf |url-status=live |journal=International Journal of Social Research Methodology |publisher=Informa UK Limited |volume=23 |issue=5 |pages=525–531 |doi=10.1080/13645579.2020.1768343 |issn=1364-5579 |s2cid=219468104 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511155452/https://eprints.bbk.ac.uk/id/eprint/31812/10/31812a.pdf |archive-date=11 May 2022 |access-date=3 April 2022}}</ref><ref name="Hines pp. 533–538">{{cite journal |last=Hines |first=Sally |date=21 May 2020 |title=Counting the cost of difference: a reply to Sullivan |journal=International Journal of Social Research Methodology |publisher=Informa UK Limited |volume=23 |issue=5 |pages=533–538 |doi=10.1080/13645579.2020.1768344 |issn=1364-5579 |s2cid=219460085}}</ref><ref name="Rodger 2021">{{cite web |last=Rodger |first=Hannah |date=4 April 2021 |title=Hundreds of academics back self-ID sex question in Scottish census |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/19208054.hundreds-academics-back-self-id-sex-question-scottish-census/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210911152129/https://www.heraldscotland.com/news/19208054.hundreds-academics-back-self-id-sex-question-scottish-census/ |archive-date=11 September 2021 |access-date=11 September 2021 |website=HeraldScotland}}</ref> for example, on the ground that the transgender population is very small.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Counting Trans Populations {{!}} Division of Prevention Science |url=https://prevention.ucsf.edu/transhealth/education/data-recs-summary |access-date=25 March 2023 |website=prevention.ucsf.edu |archive-date=13 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220513105623/https://prevention.ucsf.edu/transhealth/education/data-recs-summary |url-status=live }}</ref> 

==== Position in Scotland ====
In Scotland, similar pieces of guidance have been published since the previous census in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sex question recommendation report |url=https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/documents/sex-question-recommendation-report/ |access-date=26 March 2023 |website=Scotland's Census |language=en}}</ref> The Scottish Parliament also sought to amend the census Act in 2019 to clarify the meaning of sex in that legislation to include gender identity. The plan was abandoned and changes were instead made in subordinate legislation. In August 2021, [[National Records of Scotland]] issued guidelines regarding the sex question in the 2022 Scottish census. The guidance states that "If you are transgender the answer you give can be different from what is on your birth certificate. You do not need a Gender Recognition Certificate (GRC)". The [[UK Statistics Authority]] wrote to National Records of Scotland to question the guidelines.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Horne|first=Marc|date=17 September 2021|title=Watchdog queries trans self-identify census plan|work=[[The Times]]|url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/watchdog-queries-trans-self-identify-census-plan-5bdv923xk|access-date=17 September 2021|archive-date=17 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210917083330/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/watchdog-queries-trans-self-identify-census-plan-5bdv923xk|url-status=live}}</ref>

In November 2021, the Murray Blackburn Mackenzie (MBM) policy collective claimed that documents obtained via the [[Freedom of Information Act 2000|Freedom of Information Act]] showed that the [[Equality and Human Rights Commission]] put "extreme external pressure" on Scottish civil servants including chief statistician Roger Halliday to amend their initial proposals.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Watson|first=Jeremy|date=4 November 2021|title=Equality and Human Rights Commission had 'heavy-handed' influence on gender questions|work=[[The Times]]|url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/equality-and-human-rights-commission-had-heavy-handed-influence-on-gender-question-in-census-mwlgh5ls7|access-date=4 November 2021|archive-date=4 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211104085012/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/equality-and-human-rights-commission-had-heavy-handed-influence-on-gender-question-in-census-mwlgh5ls7|url-status=live}}</ref>

In December 2021, Fair Play for Women applied for a judicial review in Scotland. [[Craig Sandison, Lord Sandison|Lord Sandison]] dismissed the case on 17 February 2022 stating that there was "no general rule or principle of law that a question as to a person's sex may only properly be answered by reference to the sex stated on that person's birth certificate or [[Gender Recognition Act 2004|GRC]]".<ref>{{cite news |last=Pease |first=Victoria |date=17 February 2022 |title=Legal challenge by women's group over census sex question thrown out |work=[[STV (TV channel)]] |url=https://news.stv.tv/politics/lord-sandison-throws-out-fair-play-for-women-legal-challenge-over-census-sex-question |access-date=18 February 2022 |archive-date=18 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218003536/https://news.stv.tv/politics/lord-sandison-throws-out-fair-play-for-women-legal-challenge-over-census-sex-question |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Carrell |first=Severin |date=17 February 2022 |title=Transgender people can self-identify in Scottish census, confirms judge |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2022/feb/17/transgender-people-can-self-identify-in-scottish-census-confirms-judge |access-date=18 February 2022 |archive-date=18 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218003534/https://www.theguardian.com/society/2022/feb/17/transgender-people-can-self-identify-in-scottish-census-confirms-judge |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=<!--Staff writer(s)/no by-line.--> |title=Legal challenge to Scottish census sex question thrown out |date=17 February 2022 |access-date=18 February 2022 |work=[[BBC News]] |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-60420339 |archive-date=18 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218003533/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-60420339 |url-status=live }}</ref>

An appeal by Fair Play for Women was refused by the Inner House of the [[Court of Session]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mulholland |first1=James |title=Court appeal over census sex question rejected by judges 24 February 2022 |date=24 February 2022 |url=https://news.stv.tv/scotland/scottish-judges-rule-transgender-people-can-self-identify-sex-in-upcoming-census?amp |publisher=stv news |access-date=27 February 2022 |archive-date=27 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220227120812/https://news.stv.tv/scotland/scottish-judges-rule-transgender-people-can-self-identify-sex-in-upcoming-census?amp |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Coordination ===

The UK Statistics Authority has the responsibility for coordinating the census arrangements across the United Kingdom through the [[Office for National Statistics]] (ONS), which is also responsible for the census in England and Wales.

=== 2021 census research ===

The [[UK census 2011|2011 UK census]] was the first decennial census in the United Kingdom to include the option of completing the census documentation online. Across the UK between 15 and 19% of census forms were submitted online.<ref name="NIrecommendation">[http://www.nisra.gov.uk/census/2021.html The Future Provision of Census of Population Information for Northern Ireland NISRA] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230213657/http://www.nisra.gov.uk/census/2021.html |date=30 December 2014 }}, Accessed 30 December 2014</ref><ref>[http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/guide-method/census/2011/how-our-census-works/how-did-we-do-in-2011-/internet-take-up-rates---final---with-country-totals.xls 2011 Census: Percentage of individual returns via paper and internet questionnaires in England] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230213313/http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/guide-method/census/2011/how-our-census-works/how-did-we-do-in-2011-/internet-take-up-rates---final---with-country-totals.xls |date=30 December 2014 }}, Accessed 30 December 2014</ref> The UK Statistics Authority proposed that the 2021 census should be conducted predominantly online (with support provided for those unable to complete the census online), supplemented by the use of administrative and survey data and improve annual statistics between censuses.<ref name="2021recommendation"/> For the census in 2021 the proposed target for online completion has been set to at least 65%.<ref>[http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/reports-and-publications/beyond-2011-research-conference-2014--summary-of-proceedings.pdf Beyond 2011 Research Conference 2014: Summary of proceedings ONS] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903120913/http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/reports-and-publications/beyond-2011-research-conference-2014--summary-of-proceedings.pdf |date=3 September 2014 }}, Accessed 30 December 2014</ref>

Research has been under way since 2011 to design a new census methodology which maximises the success of an online approach.

Research commissioned by the Beyond 2011 programme identified that there were risks associated with over-reliance on administrative data drawn from governmental department sources due to process changes, such as benefits and welfare payments and the necessity to include full access to statistical data as part as proposed legislation affecting administrative programmes. Issues identified also included the accuracy of administrative data sets for geographical areas below that of local authorities, problems associated with estimation and the use of address registers. ONS on behalf of the UK Statistics Authority has taken on board the recommendations of the Skinner Report into methodology work and has proposed three research strands to determine the 'optimum blend' of online census, administrative data and surveying methods for the 2021 census and indeed subsequent censuses.<ref>[http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/reports-and-publications/methods-and-policies-reports/beyond-2011--ons-response-to-recommendations-from-the-independent-review-of-methodology.pdf Beyond 2011: Independent Review of Methodology ONS] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140508122912/http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/reports-and-publications/methods-and-policies-reports/beyond-2011--ons-response-to-recommendations-from-the-independent-review-of-methodology.pdf |date=8 May 2014 }}, Accessed 30 December 2014</ref>

The UK Statistics Authority has commissioned research strands as part of a census transformation programme which was due to report by 2017 relating to the 2021 census operation, the shape of population statistics in 2021, and the shape of population statistics beyond 2021 in the lead up to 2031.<ref>[http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/faqs/index.html#2 FAQ Census Transformation Programme] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141007142448/http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/about-ons/who-ons-are/programmes-and-projects/beyond-2011/faqs/index.html#2 |date=7 October 2014 }}, Accessed 25 January 2015</ref>

=== Census work programme ===

A work programme running until 2024, comprising eight phases, was developed by ONS.<ref>[http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/guide-method/census/analysis/user-engagement/census-analysis-workshop-cardiff-november-2014/ann-blake.ppt Planning for 2021 – slides 15/17 – ONS Powerpoint Presentation November 2014] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231030335/http://www.ons.gov.uk/ons/guide-method/census/analysis/user-engagement/census-analysis-workshop-cardiff-november-2014/ann-blake.ppt |date=31 December 2014 }}, Accessed 30 December 2014</ref>
# Research (ended March 2015)
# Design and prototyping (ended December 2016)
# Testing (2017)
# Development (2018)
# Rehearsal (January 2019 – June 2020)
# Collection operations (July 2020 – December 2021)
# Analysis, output and dissemination (2022–23)
# Evaluation / future planning (2023–24)

Alongside this programme trials of statistics generation using administrative data were planned starting from the autumn of 2015 and running through to 2021 with the aim of ranging across the breadth, detail and accuracy of census outputs.

=== Production ===

The contract for preparing, dispatching up to 16 million paper questionnaire packs (for anyone who did not want to, or could not access the census online), and then securely managing, capturing and digitising the responses was awarded to [[Leidos|Leidos Innovations UK]]. The contract was estimated to be worth around £65.1m.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Leidos to support the 2021 Census for England, Wales and Northern Ireland|url=https://www.leidos.com/insights/leidos-support-2021-census-england-wales-and-northern-ireland|access-date=13 February 2021|website=Leidos|language=en|archive-date=24 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210224135219/https://www.leidos.com/insights/leidos-support-2021-census-england-wales-and-northern-ireland|url-status=live}}</ref> The parent company of Leidos Innovations UK, Leidos (an American defence, aviation, information technology, and biomedical research company), merged with Lockheed Martin's IT sector in August 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lockheed Martin Successfully Closes Transaction to Separate and Combine IT and Technical Services Businesses with Leidos|url=https://news.lockheedmartin.com/2016-08-16-Lockheed-Martin-Successfully-Closes-Transaction-to-Separate-and-Combine-IT-and-Technical-Services-Businesses-with-Leidos|access-date=13 February 2021|website=Media - Lockheed Martin|language=en-us|archive-date=30 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210130215201/https://news.lockheedmartin.com/2016-08-16-Lockheed-Martin-Successfully-Closes-Transaction-to-Separate-and-Combine-IT-and-Technical-Services-Businesses-with-Leidos|url-status=live}}</ref> Lockheed Martin UK was awarded the contract for the census in 2011.<ref>{{Cite press release|last=Martin|first=Lockheed|title=UK's Office For National Statistics And Lockheed Martin UK Successfully Deliver UK Census|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/uks-office-for-national-statistics-and-lockheed-martin-uk-successfully-deliver-uk-census-166253946.html|access-date=13 February 2021|website=Prnewswire.com|language=en|archive-date=24 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220224202314/https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/uks-office-for-national-statistics-and-lockheed-martin-uk-successfully-deliver-uk-census-166253946.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
[[The Adecco Group|Adecco UK]] was contracted by ONS to recruit, train and administer the pay for the 30,000 temporary ONS workers who would be working as field staff for the 2021 census.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|title=The ONS Appoints the Adecco Group UK&I to Staff the 2021 Census Team|url=https://www.prnewswire.co.uk/news-releases/the-ons-appoints-the-adecco-group-uk-amp-i-to-staff-the-2021-census-team-868878017.html|access-date=13 February 2021|website=Prnewswire.co.uk|language=en|archive-date=17 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210417090417/https://www.prnewswire.co.uk/news-releases/the-ons-appoints-the-adecco-group-uk-amp-i-to-staff-the-2021-census-team-868878017.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Changes from 2011 census ===

The general style of the questionnaire was similar to that of the [[2011 Census for England and Wales|2011 census]], although there were some new questions for 2021:

* Are the respondents ex-armed forces?<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Barton|first=Cassie|date=13 February 2021|title=Preparing for the 2021 census (England and Wales)|url=https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-8531/|language=en-GB|journal=|access-date=13 February 2021|archive-date=7 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210207110028/https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/cbp-8531/|url-status=live}}</ref>
* Voluntary question for 16 and over about sexual orientation.<ref name=":1" />
* Voluntary question for 16 and over: Is the gender you identify with the same as your sex registered at birth? This is in addition to the compulsory question about respondents' sex.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Barton|first=Cassie|date=|title=Preparing for the 2021 census (England and Wales)|url=https://researchbriefings.files.parliament.uk/documents/CBP-8531/CBP-8531.pdf|journal=Parliament Research|volume=|pages=|via=|access-date=13 February 2021|archive-date=16 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816211734/https://researchbriefings.files.parliament.uk/documents/CBP-8531/CBP-8531.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Advertising ===

An advertising campaign (made under contract by [[M&C Saatchi]]) was launched under the slogan of "it's about us" at the start of 2021. Television adverts tried to show a diverse range of people in various locations in England and Wales in front of a purple fabric screen, with a cover version of [[The Zombies]]' "[[This Will Be Our Year]]", performed by Jose McGill & The Vagaband, featuring as the advert soundtrack.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Office for National Statistics: It's about us by M&C Saatchi|url=https://www.thedrum.com/creative-works/project/mc-saatchi-the-office-national-statistics-its-about-us|access-date=13 February 2021|website=The Drum|language=en|archive-date=12 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210212214449/https://www.thedrum.com/creative-works/project/mc-saatchi-the-office-national-statistics-its-about-us|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Hardy|first=Ben|date=12 February 2021|title=Norwich band perform in national census advert|url=https://www.edp24.co.uk/news/norwich-band-the-vagaband-in-census-advert-7322046|access-date=13 February 2021|website=Eastern Daily Press|language=en-UK|archive-date=12 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210212205427/https://www.edp24.co.uk/news/norwich-band-the-vagaband-in-census-advert-7322046|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=M&C Saatchi campaign for 2021 UK census features more than 200 members of public|url=https://www.campaignlive.co.uk/article/m-c-saatchi-campaign-2021-uk-census-features-200-members-public/1707147|access-date=13 February 2021|website=Campaignlive.co.uk|archive-date=12 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210212112003/https://www.campaignlive.co.uk/article/m-c-saatchi-campaign-2021-uk-census-features-200-members-public/1707147|url-status=live}}</ref>

The [[Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency]] (NISRA) undertakes the census in Northern Ireland.<ref name="2021recommendation" />

The NISRA has published a report reviewing the 2011 census and other online-orientated censuses abroad and identified the importance of such things as pre-census publicity, the use of a unique internet code or ePin, and a coordinated promotion and follow up process during the census completion period.<ref name="NIrecommendation" />

The [[National Records of Scotland]] (NRS) is responsible for the census in [[Scotland]].<ref name="establishingNRS">About Us, National Records of Scotland [https://www.nrscotland.gov.uk/about-us] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004185759/https://www.nrscotland.gov.uk/about-us|date=4 October 2018}}, Accessed 4 October 2018</ref> A rehearsal was conducted on 7 October 2019 and closed for returns on 7 November 2019 in three local authority areas: parts of [[Glasgow City Council|Glasgow City]], [[Dumfries and Galloway]] and [[Na h-Eileanan Siar]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Census Rehearsal 2019 {{!}} Scotland's Census|url=https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/census-rehearsal-2019|access-date=4 February 2021|website=Scotlandscensus.gov.uk|archive-date=17 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210117153316/https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/census-rehearsal-2019|url-status=live}}</ref>

The census was scheduled to take place on 21 March 2021, but was delayed in July 2020 by the [[Scottish Government]] because of the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{Cite news|date=17 July 2020|title=Coronavirus: Census delayed by a year because of disease|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-53444651|access-date=4 February 2021|archive-date=18 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210218102801/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-53444651|url-status=live}}</ref>

The [[Scottish Government]] has come under criticism for the way the census has been conducted, with some news outlets describing the results as being "botched" due to record low turnout rates<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |date=31 May 2022 |title=Call for inquiry over Scotland's census 'fiasco' |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-scotland-politics-61637371 |access-date=7 December 2022 |archive-date=7 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221207172602/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-scotland-politics-61637371 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Pooran |first=Neil |title=Audit Scotland confirms botched census will cost millions more |newspaper=[[The Times]] |language=en |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/audit-scotland-confirms-botched-census-will-cost-millions-more-qnl5dltpj |access-date=7 December 2022 |issn=0140-0460}}</ref> and failing to meet the set target return rate of 94%.<ref>{{Cite news |date=29 November 2022 |title=Lessons must be learned on low census rate - report |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-63797117 |access-date=7 December 2022 |archive-date=7 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221207172557/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-63797117 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite news |last=Pooran |first=Neil |title=Census data still useful, says adviser |newspaper=[[The Times]] |language=en |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/article/census-data-still-useful-says-adviser-rpm5vkvpf |access-date=7 December 2022 |issn=0140-0460 |archive-date=10 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250410103951/https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/article/census-data-still-useful-says-adviser-rpm5vkvpf |url-status=live }}</ref> Initial turnout rates for the census in Scotland concluded with 79% return rate; an additional round of extension to filling out the census was granted to encourage returns,<ref>{{Cite news |date=28 April 2022 |title=Scottish census deadline extended after poor response |language=en-GB |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-61255699 |access-date=7 December 2022 |archive-date=7 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221207172810/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-scotland-61255699 |url-status=live }}</ref> raising the return rate percentage to 89%.<ref name=":3" /> The return rate for comparison in England and Wales was 97%.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2" /> However national statistician [[Ian Diamond]] has said that despite not meeting the target, the census could still provide "really good data".<ref name=":4" /> The additional round of extension cost the Scottish Government an additional £6m,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Smith |first=Mark |title=Scotland's census closes 6% short after spending £6m on extension |newspaper=[[The Times]] |language=en |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/article/scotlands-census-closes-6-short-after-spending-6m-on-extension-nlctbktgj |access-date=7 December 2022 |issn=0140-0460 |archive-date=5 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250405092614/https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/article/scotlands-census-closes-6-short-after-spending-6m-on-extension-nlctbktgj |url-status=live }}</ref> and £148m in total.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tiwari |first=Vidushi |date=29 November 2022 |title='Lessons must be learned' after 2022 census costs Scotland £148m |url=https://news.stv.tv/scotland/census-lessons-must-be-learned-after-significantly-low-return-rate-says-auditor-general-of-scotland |access-date=7 December 2022 |website=STV News |language=en-GB |archive-date=7 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221207172558/https://news.stv.tv/scotland/census-lessons-must-be-learned-after-significantly-low-return-rate-says-auditor-general-of-scotland |url-status=live }}</ref>
{{clear}}

== Censuses in Crown Dependencies ==

Although it is a [[Crown Dependency]] and not part of the United Kingdom, [[Jersey]] carried out a census on the same day as the 2021 censuses in England and Wales, and Northern Ireland.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gov.je/Government/Census/Pages/Census2021.aspx |title=Census 2021 |publisher=Government of Jersey |accessdate=16 November 2020 |archive-date=26 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220626023214/https://www.gov.je/government/census/censusjersey/Pages/home.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[Guernsey]] no longer carries out a decennial census, instead using the Rolling Electronic Census Project to produce regular census reports.<ref>{{cite web |title=Population, Employment and Earnings |date=31 January 2018 |url=https://www.gov.gg/population |publisher=States of Guernsey |accessdate=16 November 2020 |archive-date=14 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210214205021/https://www.gov.gg/population |url-status=live }}</ref>

The [[Isle of Man]] also undertook a full census in 2021 (having held an interim census in 2016).<ref>{{cite web |title=Census |url=https://www.gov.im/census/ |publisher=Isle of Man Government |accessdate=16 November 2020 |archive-date=23 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923233858/https://www.gov.im/census/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Results ==
===England and Wales===
Initial results, released in June 2022, showed the recorded population of England and Wales to be 59,597,300 (56,489,800 in England and 3,107,500 in Wales), a rise of 6.3% or 3.5 million people over the previous decade. This was the largest population ever recorded through a census in England and Wales, and the overall population of the United Kingdom was estimated to be 67 million. The census also showed that the population of the two countries, aged 65 and over, had surpassed the number of children aged 15 and under for the first time, with 11.1 million people aged 65 and over compared with 10.4 million aged under 15.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-61966084|title=Census: Population of England and Wales grew 6% in a decade|date=28 June 2022|work=BBC News|access-date=28 June 2022}}</ref>

Results of the question on religion were published on 29 November 2022. The question was voluntary but was answered by 94.0% of the population of England and Wales. 46.2% of the population described themselves as "[[Christians|Christian]]", 6.5% as "[[Islam in the United Kingdom|Muslim]]", and 1.7% as "[[Hinduism in the United Kingdom|Hindu]]". 37.2% of the population asserted that they had "no religion".<ref>Office for National Statistics, [https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/culturalidentity/religion/bulletins/religionenglandandwales/census2021 Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021: The religion of usual residents and household religious composition in England and Wales, Census 2021 data] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221129100449/https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/culturalidentity/religion/bulletins/religionenglandandwales/census2021 |date=29 November 2022 }}, release dated 29 November 2022, accessed 4 December 2022</ref> In Wales, there were more people declaring that they had "no religion" (47%) than those affirming a Christian identity or any other religion.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://humanists.uk/2022/11/29/more-non-religious-in-wales-than-christians-in-2021-census/|title=More Non-religious in Wales than Christians in 2021 Census|date=29 November 2022|publisher=Humanists UK|accessdate=4 December 2022|archive-date=4 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221204142811/https://humanists.uk/2022/11/29/more-non-religious-in-wales-than-christians-in-2021-census/|url-status=live}}</ref>

====Results on sexual orientation and gender identity====
Results on sexual orientation and gender identity questions were released on 6 January 2023. Similarly to the religion question, this question was voluntary but was answered by 92.5% of the population of England and Wales. 89.4% of the population described themselves as [[Heterosexuality|straight or heterosexual]], 1.5% described themselves as "Gay or lesbian", 1.3% as "[[Bisexuality|Bisexual]]" and 0.3% were described as having "[an]other sexual orientation" (with the most common being [[Pansexuality|pansexual]], [[Asexuality|asexual]] and [[queer]]). The remaining 7.5% did not answer.<ref name=2021GenderEandW>{{cite web |title=Gender identity, England and Wales: Census 2021 |date=6 January 2023 |work=[[United Kingdom Census 2021]] |publisher=[[Office for National Statistics]] |url=https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/culturalidentity/genderidentity/bulletins/genderidentityenglandandwales/census2021 |access-date=14 May 2023 |quote=A total of 262,000 people (0.5%) answered "No", indicating that their gender identity was different from their sex registered at birth. |archive-date=19 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230519222019/https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/culturalidentity/genderidentity/bulletins/genderidentityenglandandwales/census2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> 0.5% answered 'No' to the census question 'Is the gender you identify with the same as your sex registered at birth?'<ref>{{cite web |last1=Booth and Goodier |title=England and Wales census counts trans and non-binary people for first time |date=6 January 2023 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2023/jan/06/england-and-wales-census-counts-trans-and-non-binary-people-for-first-time |website=theguardian.com |publisher=Guardian |access-date=8 January 2023 |archive-date=22 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240522041946/https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2023/jan/06/england-and-wales-census-counts-trans-and-non-binary-people-for-first-time |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Alice Sullivan]], professor of sociology at [[University College London]],<ref name=":7" /> reported that in the 16 to 24 age group, 1% answered 'No' to the question. She said that females{{Clarify|date=February 2025|reason=Females at birth or people who identify as female?}} were more likely than males to answer 'No' in that age group, whereas in other age groups females were more likely to answer 'Yes'.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Alice |date=29 January 2023 |title=What the Census reveals about trans people in Britain |url=https://www.spectator.co.uk/article/what-the-census-reveals-about-trans-people-in-britain/ |access-date=9 April 2023 |website=[[The Spectator]] |language=en-US |archive-date=9 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409155523/https://www.spectator.co.uk/article/what-the-census-reveals-about-trans-people-in-britain/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In April 2023, when more granular data became available, Michael Biggs, professor of sociology at the [[University of Oxford]],<ref name=":7" /> complained about what he perceived to be anomalies in the data on the 0.5% who identified as transgender, when disaggregated by local authority and other factors.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Biggs |first=Michael |date=9 April 2023 |title=Why does the census say there are more trans people in Newham than Brighton? |url=https://www.spectator.co.uk/article/why-does-the-census-say-there-are-more-trans-people-in-newham-than-brighton/ |access-date=9 April 2023 |website=[[The Spectator]] |language=en-US |archive-date=9 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409090759/https://www.spectator.co.uk/article/why-does-the-census-say-there-are-more-trans-people-in-newham-than-brighton/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He questioned whether the ONS had adequately tested the gender identity question with respondents for whom English is a second language.<ref name=":6" /> Biggs said that according to his analysis of the data, overall, people from an immigrant background, who do not speak English as their first language, were found to be five times more likely to be recorded as transgender and 1 in 67 Muslims were recorded as transgender, which he said was "not plausible".<ref name=":7"/> 

The [[Office for Statistics Regulation]] (OSR), which oversees the ONS, began an examination of Biggs' concerns about the statistics, including the reported result that 262,000<ref name=2021GenderEandW/> identify as transgender in England and Wales.<ref name=":7">{{Cite news |last=Beal |first=James |date=13 April 2023 |title=Watchdog to examine 'implausible' UK census trans figures |language=en |work=[[The Times]] |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/trans-figures-data-census-2021-uk-investigation-h668jcqrs |access-date=13 April 2023 |url-access=subscription |issn= |archive-date=12 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250112191833/https://www.thetimes.com/article/trans-figures-data-census-2021-uk-investigation-h668jcqrs |url-status=live }}</ref> Biggs said: "I'm 99 per cent sure that misinterpretation has had a significant impact in inflating the numbers."<ref name=":7" /> The ONS said that "while the question on gender identity was tested thoroughly, it is possible that individual responses were affected by different interpretations of the question."<ref name=":7" />

In September 2023, reporting initial findings of the OSR investigation, its head [[Ed Humpherson]] wrote of the ONS team responsible for "quality assurance": "with more time to look at all combinations of variables, for example looking at gender identity and ethnicity, it may have identified areas for additional probing and analysis." Humpherson added, "The communication of uncertainty should be strengthened".<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |last=Malnick |first=Edward |date=23 September 2023 |title=Census 'hugely overstated' trans population |language=en-GB |work=[[The Sunday Telegraph]] |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/politics/2023/09/23/census-hugely-overstated-trans-population/ |access-date=24 September 2023 |issn= |archive-date=23 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230923230044/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/politics/2023/09/23/census-hugely-overstated-trans-population/ |url-status=live }}</ref> An anonymous government source said they believed the number 260,000 of transgender people was "hugely overstated".<ref name=":8" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Booth |first1=Robert |title=Census records trans population in England and Wales – but accuracy is doubted|date=8 November 2023 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2023/nov/08/census-records-trans-population-in-england-and-wales-but-accuracy-is-doubted |work=The Guardian |access-date=12 November 2023}}</ref> 

In September 2024, the OSR removed official accreditation of the gender identity statistics, classifying them instead as official statistics in development.<ref>{{Cite web |title=OSR Publishes its Final Report on the Review of the Statistics Collected on Gender Identity During the England and Wales Census |url=https://osr.statisticsauthority.gov.uk/news/osr-publishes-its-final-report-on-the-review-of-the-statistics-collected-on-gender-identity-during-the-england-and-wales-census/ |access-date=2024-09-12 |website=Office for Statistics Regulation |language=en-GB |archive-date=12 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240912150021/https://osr.statisticsauthority.gov.uk/news/osr-publishes-its-final-report-on-the-review-of-the-statistics-collected-on-gender-identity-during-the-england-and-wales-census/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Melley |first1=James |title=Census may have overestimated number of trans people in England and Wales |date=13 September 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3030519849o |website=bbc.co.uk |publisher=BBC |access-date=15 September 2024 |archive-date=14 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240914201238/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3030519849o |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Northern Ireland ===
Results for Northern Ireland were published by the [[Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency]] in Spring 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Results |url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/2021-census/results |access-date=18 October 2023 |website=Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency |language=en |archive-date=2 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231202043301/https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/2021-census/results |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Scotland ===
[[National Records of Scotland]] published the first results on 14 September 2023. The results showed that Scotland's population was 5,436,600, the highest figure on record but a slower rate of population growth, 2.7% since 2011, than the previous growth of 4.6%.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scotland's Census first results |url=https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/news-and-events/scotland-s-census-first-results/ |access-date=17 May 2024 |website=Scotland's Census |language=en |archive-date=17 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240517083726/https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/news-and-events/scotland-s-census-first-results/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The first results, in May 2024, were population estimates at output areas, as well as topical data about ethnic group, national identity, language and religion. The rest of the data was published across 2024 and into 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Census outputs schedule |url=https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/about/2022-census/census-outputs-schedule/ |access-date=17 May 2024 |website=Scotland's Census |language=en |archive-date=21 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240521205443/https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/about/2022-census/census-outputs-schedule/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The low response rates (88%) compared with the rest of the UK mean that the data is only partial so does not fully reflect the state of Scotland's demographics.<ref name="s094">{{cite web | last=Macaskill | first=Mark | title=Census flaws led to a flood of calls | website=The Times and The Sunday Times | date=2022-06-25 | url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/article/census-flaws-led-to-a-flood-of-calls-vtxwz3wf3 | access-date=2025-04-16 | archive-date=19 April 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250419074849/https://www.thetimes.com/uk/scotland/article/census-flaws-led-to-a-flood-of-calls-vtxwz3wf3 | url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="s590">{{cite web | last=Simmons | first=Michael | title=Why Scotland's census blunder matters | website=The Spectator | date=2022-04-25 | url=https://www.spectator.co.uk/article/why-the-scottish-census-mistakes-matter/ | access-date=2025-04-16 | archive-date=19 April 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250419173005/https://www.spectator.co.uk/article/why-the-scottish-census-mistakes-matter/ | url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="g668">{{cite web | title='Lessons learned' review into census problems | website=BBC News | date=2023-08-14 | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-66503594 | access-date=2025-04-16 | archive-date=18 August 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250818101105/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-66503594 | url-status=live }}</ref>

====Households====
The census showed there were 2,509,300 households in Scotland with at least one usual resident.<ref name="o879">{{cite web | title=Demography and migration | website=Scotland&#x27;s Census | date=2025-03-19 | url=https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/2022-results/scotland-s-census-2022-demography-and-migration/ | access-date=2025-04-16}}</ref> This was an increase of 136,500 (5.8%) from the 2011 census.<ref name="o879"/> There were some 930,000 single person households in Scotland and over a third of all households were single person (37.1%).<ref name="o879"/>

====Migration====
The census revealed that over half a million people living in Scotland were born in the rest of the UK (563,500).<ref name="o879"/> Furthermore, that a further half a million were born outside of the UK (554,900).<ref name="o879"/> The number of people born outside of the UK had increased by 185,600 since 2011.<ref name="o879"/>

====Age====
The census showed the population as ageing, with over one million people aged 65 and over (1,091,000).<ref name="l150">{{cite web | title=Rounded population estimates | website=Scotland&#x27;s Census | date=2025-03-19 | url=https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/2022-results/scotlands-census-2022-rounded-population-estimates/ | access-date=2025-04-16 | archive-date=19 April 2025 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250419103057/https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/2022-results/scotlands-census-2022-rounded-population-estimates/ | url-status=live }}</ref> The number of people under 15 was only 832,300.<ref name="l150"/>

====Religion====
The majority of people said they had no religion.<ref name="ReligionScot">{{cite web | title=Scotland's Census 2022 - Ethnic group, national identity, language and religion | website=Scotland&#x27;s Census | date=2024 | url=https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/2022-results/scotland-s-census-2022-ethnic-group-national-identity-language-and-religion/ | access-date=2025-04-16 | archive-date=22 June 2024 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240622100825/https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/2022-results/scotland-s-census-2022-ethnic-group-national-identity-language-and-religion/ | url-status=live }}</ref> In 2022, 51.1% of people had no religion, up from 36.7% in 2011.<ref name="ReligionScot"/> Of those who were religious in 2022, 20.4% responded ‘Church of Scotland', 13.3% ‘Roman Catholic’, 5.1% 'Other Christian' and 2.2% 'Muslim'.<ref name="ReligionScot"/> Among those who selected 'Other Christian,' 72,359 people identified as [[Anglican Communion|Anglican]] or [[Episcopalian]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wayback Machine |url=https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/media/mcoacltm/census-2022-detailed-ethnic-group-country-of-birth-national-identity-main-language-and-religion-data-for-scotland-1.xlsx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241004030430/https://www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk/media/mcoacltm/census-2022-detailed-ethnic-group-country-of-birth-national-identity-main-language-and-religion-data-for-scotland-1.xlsx |archive-date=2024-10-04 |access-date=2025-08-06 |website=www.scotlandscensus.gov.uk}}</ref>

====Ethnicity====
In 2022 the census results showed 12.9% of people in Scotland had a minority ethnic background.<ref name="ReligionScot"/> This is an increase from 8.2% in 2011.<ref name="ReligionScot"/> 77.7% described themselves as 'Scottish', 9.4% as 'Other British'.<ref name="ReligionScot"/> The next three largest groups were 'Other White' (2.92%), 'Polish' (1.67%) and 'Pakistani' (1.34%).<ref name="ReligionScot"/>
